nary_nodes.label: Microsoft cuts 4,800 jobs
evidence: Microsoft has announced it has cut 4,800 jobs - roughly 2.1% of its workforce - with Xbox to bear a large number of its latest layoffs.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox axes 1,600 roles
evidence: The sweeping layoffs will see more than 1,600 roles immediately axed at Xbox.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox reduces another 1,600 roles
evidence: Another 1,600 roles will be reduced from Xbox as a result.

nary_nodes.label: Four Xbox studios spun off
evidence: Four Xbox game development studios - Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory and Undead Lab - would also be spun off as part of the changes, she added.

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine and Compulsion become independent
evidence: Double Fine and Compulsion will both return to independent management.

nary_nodes.label: Studios depart with IP
evidence: Both itself and Compulsion, which developed action-adventure title South of Midnight, will depart with their intellectual property (IP).

nary_nodes.label: Microsoft hikes console prices
evidence: The spiralling costs of hardware have also prompted firms including Microsoft to hike the price of years-old consoles and similar consumer gadgets - with many blaming AI data centres for pushing up demand too quickly for supply to catch up.

nary_nodes.label: Microsoft increases AI spending
evidence: Little more than a year later, Microsoft said it would cut up to 9,000 jobs after setting out plans to double down on its multi-billion-dollar AI spending.

nary_nodes.label: Coleman: focus on customer-delivering areas
evidence: Amy Coleman, executive vice president at Microsoft, told employees in a memo that the tech giant needed to focus on areas that can deliver for customers amid a "fast-changing industry".

nary_nodes.label: Sharma: biggest Xbox restructure
evidence: Asha Sharma, who recently took over as Xbox's chief executive, said in a note to staff it was "beginning the most significant restructure in Xbox history".

nary_nodes.label: Sharma: changes for bigger future
evidence: "These changes are about a bigger future for Xbox, not a smaller one," Sharma said in a note, shared on X.

nary_nodes.label: Sharma: avoid inevitability
evidence: "History is full of companies that mistake longevity for inevitability. We will not be one of them."

nary_nodes.label: Coleman: adapt to industry changes
evidence: "Companies don't get to choose whether their industry changes; they only get to choose whether they change with it," she said.

nary_nodes.label: Coleman: AI changes work
evidence: She noted that while the company would not replace the lost roles with AI, "what is true is that AI is changing how work gets done".

nary_nodes.label: Pescatore: major reset
evidence: Tech analyst Paolo Pescatore told the BBC the changes indeed marked a "major reset" for the company, which has further trials ahead.

nary_nodes.label: Harding-Rolls: restructuring underlines vision
evidence: Piers Harding-Rolls of Ampere Analysis said this restructuring "underlines Xbox's vision for its studios and content, which will be more heavily focused on the biggest IP and audiences".

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine: thankful for seven years
evidence: Double Fine, acquired by Microsoft in 2019, wrote on X that it was "thankful to everyone at Xbox for seven great years together".

nary_nodes.label: Compulsion: support team during transition
evidence: "Our immediate priority is to support our team throughout this transition period," Compulsion said on X - adding it was confident in its future.

nary_nodes.label: Sharma: painful cuts need reset
evidence: Sharma said on Monday that while she knew the cuts were "painful", there was a "reset" needed across Xbox's entire content portfolio, platform and operations.

nary_nodes.label: Microsoft cuts up to 9,000 jobs
evidence: Little more than a year later, Microsoft said it would cut up to 9,000 jobs after setting out plans to double down on its multi-billion-dollar AI spending.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox cuts more than 2,000 staff in 2024
evidence: In 2024, Xbox culled more than 2,000 staff and shuttered four studios bought prior to its bumper acquisition of Call of Duty maker Activision-Blizzard.

nary_nodes.label: Xbox shuttered four studios
evidence: In 2024, Xbox culled more than 2,000 staff and shuttered four studios bought prior to its bumper acquisition of Call of Duty maker Activision-Blizzard.

nary_nodes.label: Pescatore: challenge defining Xbox's purpose
evidence: The challenge is not just cutting costs; it is defining what Xbox stands for in a world where games are moving across console, PC, cloud and subscription platforms," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Harding-Rolls: bought many studios to boost Game Pass
evidence: He said the company had previously bought a plethora of studios to boost offerings on its subscription service Game Pass.

nary_nodes.label: Harding-Rolls: some teams better suited outside Xbox
evidence: But the company has now decided that some of these teams and the games they are building would be better suited to sit outside the Xbox organisation," he said - adding that its decision not close them was "positive news during a difficult time".

nary_nodes.label: Double Fine: outcome preserves history and returns ownership
evidence: The Psychonauts developer added it was grateful to have been able to reach an outcome 'which preserves our history and culture, and returns ownership of our games to us'.

type_definitions.definition: An organization that engages in commercial, industrial, or professional activities.
A distinct business unit or brand within a larger company that focuses on video game products and services.
An individual human being.
A company or team that develops video games.
A non‑physical offering provided to customers, often digital.
A system of tools, methods, or processes used to achieve a technical goal.
A numeric amount representing a count or measure.
A proportion expressed as parts per hundred.
A point or span of time identified by a calendar date or relative expression.
An occurrence where a company reduces its workforce through job cuts.
An organized change to a company's internal structure, often involving studio spin‑offs or reorganization.
An event where a team or studio changes its reporting line to a different manager or executive.
An occurrence where a studio becomes independent from its parent organization.
An event where a studio departs while retaining its intellectual property.
An occurrence where a company raises the price of its products.
An event where a company raises its investment in a particular area, such as AI.
A statement attributing a strategic focus or priority to a company.
A claim describing the magnitude or importance of a restructuring effort.
A statement expressing a forward‑looking vision or goal.
A claim emphasizing the need to avoid complacency despite long existence.
A statement that stresses the necessity to adapt to changing conditions.
A claim about the influence of artificial intelligence on work or processes.
A statement that a major reset or overhaul is occurring.
A claim that a restructuring supports or clarifies a company's vision.
A statement expressing gratitude for past collaboration or support.
A claim stating that supporting the team is an immediate priority.
A claim that a painful situation necessitates a reset.
A claim expressing a strategic challenge faced by an organization.
A claim about a company's acquisition strategy to support a service or product.
A claim explaining the rationale behind a restructuring decision.
A claim describing how an outcome preserves history, culture, or ownership.
An event representing the closure of a studio or business unit.
